subject: Harbor Financial: evidence handoff and network demarcation package
messages:
From: John Miller <john.miller@harborfinancial.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@harborfinancial.com
Cc: Harbor Financial Security <security@harborfinancial.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: RFI follow-up: network demarcation, signed traces, and threat model summary

Rafael,

Thanks for the quick demo earlier this week. Harbor's Security team is doing a deeper intake for inference workloads and the procurement team asked us to collect a few concrete artifacts so we can close the RFP security checklist. Can you provide the following by next week?

- A concise network demarcation diagram (annotated, SVG/PDF) that shows control plane, data plane, operator access, and any bastion/egress points.
- Signed control-plane handshake traces (TLS negotiation summaries) or equivalent non-repudiation logs for a recent sample window.
- A short threat-model summary (1–2 pages) focussed on cross-tenant egress, sidecar failure modes, and attacker-lateralization mitigations.
- Any evidence of encrypted KV/cache handling in transit and at rest.

We may ask for redacted logs — procurement will handle any NDA details. If we can get a preliminary package and a short call to walk through it, that would help accelerate review.

Appreciate it,
John Miller
Security Program Manager
Harbor Financial
john.miller@harborfinancial.com

---
Note: procurement may also want an itemized list of where artifacts came from (S3 path, GCS bucket, or internal artifact store).
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: John Miller <john.miller@harborfinancial.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 16:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI follow-up: network demarcation, signed traces, and threat model summary

John — thanks, this is clear and actionable. We'll assemble a minimal evidence packet that matches what you've asked for. Proposed plan: 

1) Deliverables by EOD Tuesday (2027-05-25): annotated topology SVG/PDF, a redacted bundle of control-plane handshake traces, and a 1–2 page threat summary.
2) Provide a short provenance checklist listing artifact locations and owners (for procurement).
3) Quick walkthrough call (30 min) on Wednesday morning (your time) after you've had a chance to scan the package.

Ben and Kim — can you own artifact collection and redaction? Marissa — can you run the final QA + packaging and upload to the Drive folder below once complete? We'll include the signed-trace artifacts, but we should confirm the format Harbor prefers (PDF summary + CSV traces or a single zip).

Drive (working folder): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C4dHarborEvidence
Jira: SEC-4372 (for internal tracking)

If any of the items above would violate policy/PII concerns, flag immediately and we'll coordinate.

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Director, Solutions Security
Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: rafael.mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI follow-up: network demarcation, signed traces, and threat model summary

Rafael — I'll pull the handshake traces from the control-plane bucket and produce the CSV summary. Kimberly, key items for redaction: operator usernames, internal IPs that map to customer test beds, and any JWTs. I'll include a hashed identifier column so Harbor can correlate without seeing raw tokens.

Quick note on the topology: our recommended minimal demarcation diagram will show three logical zones:  

  - Control plane: management API, certificate authorities, operator services (isolated, private control subnet)
  - Data plane: inference runtime + model hosts (tenant network, per-tenant workload isolation)
  - Operator access / egress: bastionless jumpbox (optional) with egress filtering and explicit NAT/egress gateways

Tiny ascii sketch to justify the visual: 

  [Operator Console] -- TLS --> [Control Plane API] =====VPN/TLS===== [Data Plane Runtime Cluster] --(KV/cache TLS)--> [Persistent Stores]

Threat focus: egress from Data Plane to operator-controlled endpoints, KV cache exposure if sidecar fails to enforce per-tenant keys, and fallback model variants that widen attack surface. I'll draft the 1–2 page summary and attach to the evidence packet.

I'll start export now and hand off to Marissa for QA.

Ben
Senior Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs referenced: controlplane-handshake-traces.csv (sample), topology-lightweight.svg (diagram source), initial-thrust-threat-notes.txt
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: packaging checklist and redaction guidance for Harbor packet

Team — status update and checklist before we hand off to John: 

- controlplane-handshake-traces.csv: exported and truncated to a 24-hour window (Ben). Include signature verification hashes; do not include full TLS private keys.
- topology-lightweight.svg + topology-lightweight.pdf: diagram annotated with demarcation labels (Ben/Marissa).
- threat-summary-redacted.pdf: 1.5 pages, redactions applied for internal hostnames (Kimberly).
- harbor_rfi_network_evidence.zip: final bundle that will include the above plus a small provenance.txt that lists artifacts and S3 paths (redwood-internal://controlplane/exports/harbor/2027-05-24).

Marissa — please confirm redaction checklist: 
  - remove operator usernames and replace with hashed IDs
  - scrub internal CIDR references that map to customer test environments
  - verify that control-plane logs do not contain customer PII

Once QA passes, upload to the Drive folder and flag John with the package link. If procurement needs a signed manifest, we can generate one with the S3 manifest + a SHA256 list.

Thanks — Rafael

Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Harbor Financial — deliverables: topology, signed-trace samples, and threat summary (package)

Hi John / Harbor team —

Attached is the evidence packet we prepared per your request. Summary of what's included: 

- harbor_rfi_network_evidence.zip (contains topology-lightweight.pdf, controlplane-handshake-traces.csv, threat-summary-redacted.pdf, provenance.txt)
- controlplane-handshake-traces.csv — contains a 24-hour sample of TLS negotiation summaries and signature hashes (all sensitive fields redacted or hashed).
- topology-lightweight.svg / PDF — annotated demarcation diagram (control plane, data plane, operator access, egress).
- threat-summary-redacted.pdf — 1.5 page summary of attacker paths and mitigations, with redactions for internal hostnames.

Drive link (read-only): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C4dHarborEvidence
Internal ticket: https://redwoodinference.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-4372
DocuSign manifest (if procurement requires): https://www.docusign.net/Harbor/Envelope/123456789

Notes on provenance: provenance.txt inside the zip lists the S3/object store locations and the SHA256 manifest for each artifact. We did not include private keys or unredacted operator sessions. If you need signed attestation (PKCS7) for any of the artifacts, let us know and we will route to our compliance team.

Next steps: can we schedule a 30-minute walkthrough on Wednesday 2027-05-26 at 10:00 AM ET to talk through any clarifications?

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Director, Solutions Security
Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com
